html:
From the 1890s the gold mines of the Witwatersrand recruited huge numbers of men from southern Mozambique, through an agency later called the Witwatersrand Native Labour Association.

Portugal made deals with the Transvaal and then South Africa: the mines got workers, and in return a share of the Transvaal's trade went through the port of Lourenço Marques, and part of the miners' wages was paid in gold to Portugal. At times over a hundred thousand Mozambicans worked on the mines.

Mine wages paid for bride wealth, ploughs and cattle in the south, and many men spent most of their working lives away. The flow was cut after independence, but still continues. It tied Mozambique to the gold of the Rand.
sum: From the 1890s the gold mines of the Witwatersrand recruited huge numbers of men from southern Mozambique, through an agency later called the Witwatersrand Native Labour Association.
